newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Kidnapped Colombian newspaper editor freed.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped Colombian newspaper editor freed.

text.p: A kidnapped newspaper editor who had received death threats for his hard-hitting columns has been freed unharmed in northern Colombia, police said on Thursday.

Ulido Acevedo Silva, 38, editor and founder of the Hoy Diario del Magdalena newspaper, was released late on Wednesday, five days after he was abducted near his office in the Caribbean coast port of Santa Marta.
A police spokesman said no ransom was paid.
Police chief Col. Octavio Grajales said straight after Acevedo's disappearance that the editor had previously received death threats because of the themes he dealt with in his columns.
Acevedo told the Noticiero Nacional television news program on Thursday his captors did not talk about politics to him.
"I was kept handcuffed and blindfolded and a gun was held constantly at my neck," he said. "My captors did not talk to me about politics, I think they were common criminals."

Santa Marta is one of the main ports on Colombia's Caribbean coast. Drug trafficking and smuggling is rife in the area, police sources say, and there is a heavy leftist guerrilla presence in the surrounding countryside.
